miniProject.title: Collectives, overlap and disaggregation across GPUs
miniProject.brief: Model collectives, sweep message sizes and prove overlap with two GPUs, falling back to an analytical model checked against published results with one. Size all work to fit your GPU's memory and build with `-arch=native`.
steps: Capture `nvidia-smi topo -m` and label each GPU pair with its path. With two GPUs run the staging pair and `nccl_benchmark.py`; with one GPU fit an analytical model checked against published nccl-tests results, recording blockers with dumps in both cases.

Derive bytes and step counts for ring all-gather, reduce-scatter and all-reduce, with the latency-bandwidth crossover, then build `myAllreduce` and `myAlltoall` from point-to-point calls. Check them with the CPU MPI cases plus pytest, and solve the TensorTonic collective, bandwidth, gradient-average and column-parallel MLP problems.

Build nccl-tests against your PyTorch NCCL and run `all_reduce_perf` with two GPUs across algorithms and protocols, predicting each point first. Record the NCCL version and a topology dump per number, and state the rules that overrides precede communicator creation and rank order fixes layout.

Derive the exposed time for bucketed overlap under the dependency you state. With two GPUs run `ddp_overlap.py` against `ddp_no_overlap.py` under `torchrun`, attributing the gap from rank-aligned timelines.

Collect rank-aligned timelines for one collective, name the straggler and its waiting cost, and confirm with a barrier experiment. Inject a straggler and a partial failure with two GPUs, record the abort procedure, and separate congestion from affinity with a placement swap.

Derive per-layer dispatch and combine bytes with per-expert capacity under a stated factor, and show how one hot expert changes the maximum. Measure hot-expert behavior, apply the capacity policy, and record the rebalancing decision.

Derive KV transfer time against TTFT and TPOT slack to call the disaggregation crossover. Fit latency and bandwidth terms from sweep points, predict one held-out size, and state the setup the fit depends on.
deliverables: Topology dumps with labeled paths, collective derivations with the crossover, and CPU MPI checks.
The NCCL sweep with version and dump per number, overlap attribution and straggler runs with abort records.
The MoE volume and rebalancing decision, the disaggregation crossover and the held-out fit prediction.

checks.name: CSE 291A PA2 Part 2 local MPI tests
checks.note: Run the `mpi-test.py` cases and pytest files on CPU with Open MPI and `mpi4py`; keep the `discussion2-1.txt` timing comparison.

rubric.pass: Ring derivations give bytes and steps with the crossover stated, the NCCL sweep names version and topology per number, and single-GPU runs are labeled simulation.
rubric.strong: The hierarchy sketch names which exchange crosses the slow link and why it carries less data.

rubric.pass: The exposed-time derivation states its dependency, overlap is attributed from aligned timelines, and the straggler with its waiting cost is confirmed by a barrier experiment.
rubric.strong: The partial-failure run names the abort procedure that invalidates it.

rubric.pass: MoE dispatch and combine volumes with the capacity policy support the rebalancing decision, and the crossover calls disaggregation against stated slack with transfer math.
rubric.strong: The held-out prediction is checked against measurement with the setup stated.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone communication: the NCCL sweep, overlap proof, straggler analysis, MoE decision and disaggregation crossover. The final report reuses the topology dumps and the fitted model.
